title: Consolidate host copy shards and harmonize threadpools to reduce prefill/decode overhead
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Background: Production traces show recurring spikes during prefill->decode handoff where host CPU work (copy scatter/coalesce, copy staging buffers, and short-lived threadpool tasks) becomes the critical path for tail latency at 95/99 percentiles. These spikes are exacerbated for mixed-sequence workloads where small requests interleave with long-prefix streaming.

Scope: This ticket targets three coordinated host-side changes aimed at reducing CPU-GPU pipeline overheads: (1) deterministic consolidation of memcpy paths into a small number of sharded copy lanes to avoid fan-out and cache line thrashing; (2) harmonization of the various internal threadpools (prefill, transport, work-stealing) into a unified scheduler with token-aware priorities to avoid contention and migrate lightweight tasks to a low-latency executor; (3) narrow attention-optimization hooks during prefill that allow the kernel selector to prefer fused attention kernels for short-prefix cases to reduce small-kernel launch overhead.

Goals: Reduce prefill tail latency (95/99) by >=25% on mixed workloads; cut host-side memcpy volume per request by >=30% for typical token distributions; eliminate threadpool saturation events visible on latency heatmaps. Preserve correctness, maintain existing telemetry, and provide a config toggle for gradual rollout.

Non-goals: This ticket does not rework GPU kernel internals beyond kernel selection hints, and does not change network transport layer protocols. Longer-term quantization or KV cache format changes are out of scope.
updates: 2026-02-14: Investigated flamegraphs from canary region. Observed repeated thread wakeups in transport threadpool correlated with memcpy spikes. Pinpointed three hot memcpy call sites.
2026-02-20: Experimented with single-shard memcpy path on staging; memcpy CPU time reduced ~18% on 8k-request sample but tail latency unchanged due to threadpool backpressure.
2026-02-27: Prototype unified low-latency executor (single-producer ring + work-stealing fallback). Microbenchmarks show <10us enqueue/dequeue for small tasks vs ~45us previously.

2026-03-03: Added kernel-selection hint flag for fused attention on short prefix sizes. Preliminary results: reduced kernel launch count per request by ~12% and freed up GPU SM time in 512-token workload.

2026-03-08: End-to-end staging run with combined changes: 95th latency down 22%, 99th down 28%, host memcpy bytes/request down 34%. Identified regressions for very large-batch streaming workloads (follow-up action).
2026-03-10: Created PRs for copy-path consolidation and unified executor. Requesting design review and perf sig-off before canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Combined change deployed to canary with toggle; canary perf shows >=25% reduction in 95th prefill latency for mixed workloads compared to baseline
Host memcpy bytes/request reduced by >=30% on representative traces
No increase in request-level error rate or GPU OOM events in canary (<= baseline)
Telemetry added: per-lane memcpy counters, executor queue depth heatmaps, kernel-selection decision logs
Runbook updated with rollout toggle and rollback steps
